stories.title_en: The Country Mouse and the Town Mouse
stories.why_ar: تتدرّب على الماضي البسيط وعلى المقارنة مثل bigger than وbetter than.
lines: A country mouse invited his cousin from town.
He gave him bread and seeds.
"Your food is simple," said the town mouse. "Come to my house. It is bigger than yours."
The next day they went to town.
The town house was beautiful, and the food was richer.
They ate cake, meat and fruit on a big table.
Suddenly the door opened, and a large dog ran in.
The two mice hid in a hole, afraid.
The country mouse went home the same night.
"Your food is better than mine, but my bread is safer," he said.
stories.moral_en: A simple life in peace is better than a rich life in fear.
stories.moral_ar: العيش البسيط في أمان خيرٌ من الغنى مع الخوف.

stories.why_ar: تتدرّب على الماضي البسيط، وعلى أسئلة الماضي، وعلى المقارنة مثل faster than.
lines: A monkey lived in a tree by a river, and a crocodile was his friend.
Every day the monkey gave him sweet fruit.
One day the crocodile said, "Come to my house."
The monkey sat on his back.
In the deep water, the crocodile said, "My wife wants your heart."
The monkey was afraid, but he thought fast.
"Why didn't you tell me?" he said. "My heart is in the tree!"
The crocodile swam back.
The monkey jumped up, faster than ever.
"Go home," he laughed. "You will never get it."
stories.moral_en: A quick mind is stronger than big teeth.
stories.moral_ar: العقل الحاضر أقوى من الأسنان الكبيرة.

stories.why_ar: تتدرّب على الماضي البسيط وأسئلته، وعلى الحوار القصير.
lines: Juha borrowed a big pot from his neighbor.
The next day he gave it back with a small pot inside it.
"Your pot had a baby," Juha said. The neighbor was happy and took both pots.
A week later, Juha borrowed the big pot again.
This time, he didn't bring it back.
After many days, the neighbor knocked on Juha's door.
"Where is my pot?" he asked.
"I am sorry," said Juha. "Your pot died."
"Died? A pot can't die!" the neighbor shouted.
Juha smiled. "You believed it had a baby. Why don't you believe it died?"
stories.moral_en: Don't believe a strange story only when it helps you.
stories.moral_ar: من صدّق الكذبة حين نفعته، فليصدّقها حين تضرّه.

stories.title_en: Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom
stories.source_ar: من حكايات غرب إفريقيا — أُعيدت كتابتها
stories.why_ar: تتدرّب على الماضي البسيط وعلى going to للخطط، وعلى المقارنة مثل smarter than.
lines: Long ago, Anansi the spider found all the wisdom.
He put it in a pot. "I am going to keep it all," he said.
He decided to hide it in a tall tree.
He tied the pot to his front and climbed.
But the pot was in his way, and he fell again.
His little son watched.
"Father, why don't you tie it on your back?" the boy asked.
Anansi was angry. His small son was smarter than him!
He dropped the pot, and it broke on a rock.
The wisdom flew out, and a little went to every person.
stories.moral_en: No one has all the wisdom; even a child can teach you.
stories.moral_ar: لا أحد يملك الحكمة كلّها، وقد يعلّمك طفل.

stories.why_ar: تتدرّب على المضارع التامّ وعلى should وmust، وعلى الشرط الأول: if + مضارع ثم will.
lines: The mice in an old house lived in fear of a cat.
"The cat has caught three of our friends this month," said the oldest mouse.
"We must do something. Who has an idea?"
A young mouse stood up. "I have a great plan," he said.
"We should put a bell on the cat's neck."
"If the cat comes near, we will hear the bell, and we will run."
All the mice clapped and cheered. It was a wonderful plan.
Then the oldest mouse spoke. "I have one question."
"Who is going to put the bell on the cat?"
The room became very quiet.
Everyone looked at the floor.
No one said a word.
stories.moral_en: A plan is easy to make; the hard part is doing it.

stories.title_en: The Tortoise and the Two Ducks
stories.why_ar: تتدرّب على المضارع التامّ، والجملة الموصولة بـ that، وmust، والشرط الأول.
lines: A tortoise lived in a lake with two ducks that were her friends.
One summer there was no rain, and the lake became dry.
"We have found a new lake far away," said the ducks. "Come with us."
"But I can't fly," said the tortoise.
The ducks brought a stick. "Hold it in your mouth. We will carry it."
"But you must not open your mouth. If you speak, you will fall."
They flew over a village, and the people laughed.
"Look at the silly tortoise! She flies with two ducks!"
The tortoise got angry.
"I am not silly!" she shouted, and she opened her mouth.
She fell down into the village.
The ducks flew on without her.
stories.moral_en: Some words are not worth saying; a closed mouth can save you.
stories.moral_ar: بعض الكلام لا يستحقّ أن يُقال، والصمت قد ينجّيك.

stories.source_ar: من أخبار حاتم الطائي في التراث العربي — أُعيدت كتابتها
stories.why_ar: تتدرّب على المضارع التامّ، والجملة الموصولة بـ who، وhave to.
lines: Hatim al-Tai was a man who gave everything to his guests.
He had a fine horse, famous across the desert.
A king said, "I have never seen a horse like that."
He sent two men to ask Hatim for it.
They arrived on a cold night, and Hatim had no food.
"My guests have come far," he thought. "I have to feed them."
So he cooked his horse for them.
In the morning they asked for the horse.
Hatim was sad. "You have already eaten it," he said.
"A guest who comes to my tent will never go to sleep hungry."
The men went back to the king.
"Now I understand why people love him," said the king.
stories.moral_en: True generosity gives the best it has.
stories.moral_ar: الكرم الحقّ أن تعطي أغلى ما عندك.

stories.title_en: The Lion and the Clever Rabbit
stories.source_ar: من كليلة ودمنة والبنجاتنترا — أُعيدت كتابتها
stories.why_ar: تتدرّب على المضارع التامّ، والشرط الأول، والجملة الموصولة بـ who.
lines: A cruel lion killed many animals in the forest.
The animals said, "If you stay in your cave, we will send you one animal every day."
One day it was the turn of a small rabbit.
The rabbit walked slowly and arrived late.
"Why are you late?" the lion roared. "I have waited all day!"
"Sorry," said the rabbit. "I met another lion."
"He thinks he is the king here."
The lion was furious. "Show me this lion who wants my forest!"
The rabbit took him to a deep well. "He lives there."
The lion looked down and saw a lion's face.
He roared, and the other lion roared back.
He jumped in, and he never came out.
stories.moral_en: A clever mind can beat a strong body.
